story.head: Pastrňák’s favorite opponent
paras: The Red Wings are on a five-game losing streak, and the Bruins (13-5-1) lost 5-2 to Montréal on Thursday. The Bruins played last night, and the Red Wings are rested. This is an Atlantic Division matchup, with the Bruins third (tied for eighth in the NHL) and the Wings last (tied for 25th). The Atlantic has been the strongest of the four divisions so far.

The Bruins’ record (.711) is running ahead of what their chances are worth (.562), largely thanks to their goaltending. The Red Wings have played better than their record (.425) says: their chances are worth about .562, and their finishing has held them back. If their records matched their chances, these teams would be much closer in the standings, so don’t be surprised if this one is closer than the records suggest.
In their five-game skid, the Red Wings have been outscored 18-9, including 13-7 at 5-on-5.

The Bruins (lowest) and the Red Wings (4th lowest) both leave the shooting to their forwards. The Bruins have had some of the league’s best goaltending (2nd). They also sit back rather than chase on the forecheck (2nd lowest), so the Red Wings have the edge over them on forecheck pressure. Boston has allowed 2.42 goals a game, the third fewest in the league. On the other side, the Red Wings block more shots than almost anyone (2nd), but ice the puck a lot (30th).

David Pastrňák (8 G / 16 A / 24 P in 19 GP) is carrying the Bruins’ offense, with a point in nine straight games against Detroit. Elias Lindholm (7 G / 10 A / 17 P in 19 GP) isn’t far behind. For the Red Wings, Lucas Raymond (7 G / 12 A / 19 P in 20 GP) leads the way in scoring, with eight goals in eleven games against Boston since 2023-24. Viktor Arvidsson (8 G / 7 A / 15 P in 20 GP) has a team-high eight goals.

Michael DiPietro (4-1-0 / .924 SV% in 5 GS) has been terrific for Boston and will likely start. Detroit has two options in net: John Gibson (4-7-1 / .862 SV% in 13 GS) and Daniil Tarasov (2-3-2 / .919 SV% in 6 GS). Gibson has started six of their last ten games, including the last one on Thursday, so Detroit could turn to Tarasov to give him a rest. It’s anyone’s guess who gets the net.
